title: Fifa chief sacked after criticism of Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan
byline: The Fifa chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, has been sacked after openly criticising Gianni Infantino’s ill-fated plan to sell parts of the World Cup to private investors.

title: Oil climbs as fading US-Iran peace hopes raise supply risks
byline: Oil prices rose on Tuesday as prospects receded for a deal to end the Middle ‌East war, with Iran saying it would adopt a more offensive stance and the United States ruling out extension of a ceasefire deal, heightening worries about energy supply.

title: Sri Lanka Embassy in Doha recovers over Rs. 80 million in compensation
byline: The Sri Lanka Embassy in Doha has recovered compensation amounting to more than Rs. 80.8 million on behalf of the next of kin (NoK) of Sri Lankan nationals who died in Qatar during the first seven months of 2026.

title: Applications open for 11th phase of interest-free student loan scheme
byline: Applications for the 11th phase of the Interest-Free Student Loan Scheme for students seeking higher education have opened, with the application period running from August 17 to September 27, 2026.

title: 1,090 kg of illegal veterinary medicines worth nearly Rs. 3 million destroyed
byline: A stock of 1,090 kilograms of illegal veterinary medicines worth nearly Rs. 3 million was destroyed following a joint raid conducted by the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) and the Animal Production and Health Department (DAPH).

title: Substandard vehicle spare parts worth nearly Rs. 5 mn seized in Kadawatha raid
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has seized a stock of vehicle spare parts and lubricants worth nearly Rs. 5 million during a raid on a shop along the Kadawatha-Ganemulla Road.

title: ‘Summitpura Chatu’ brought back to Sri Lanka from Oman
byline: Kankanamlage Dimuthu Chaturanga Perera, also known as “Summitpura Chatu” or “Modara Chatu,” an alleged organised crime figure wanted by Sri Lankan authorities, was brought back to Sri Lanka from Oman in the early hours of Tuesday (18) and handed over to the Colombo Crimes Division (CCD) for further investigations.

title: Extreme heat poses health risks; public urged to stay hydrated
byline: Health authorities have warned that extreme heat can pose several health risks and urged the public to take precautions to stay cool and hydrated.

title: Google plans to stop making Pixel products in China in 2027
byline: Google has told suppliers it plans to have all of its Pixel smartphones, watches and wireless earbuds produced outside of China starting next year amid ongoing Washington-Beijing tensions, Nikkei Asia has learned.

title: Two arrested with deer antlers, elephant tusk ornaments in Kuruwita raid
byline: Two persons in possession of animal body parts, including antlers, hides and ornaments made from elephant tusks, were arrested during a raid conducted by the Police Special Task Force (STF) in the Kuruwita area, the Department of Wildlife Conservation said.

title: Keheliya Rambukwella arrested
byline: Former Minister Keheliya Rambukwella has been arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) in connection with an ongoing investigation.

title: Akila Viraj granted bail
byline: Former Minister Akila Viraj Kariyawasam and an employee of his fuel station, who had been remanded over allegations of corruption, were ordered to be released on bail by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama.

title: Tri-forces step in to treat injured elephant calf amid wildlife vets’ strike
byline: Veterinary personnel from the Army, Navy and Air Force have stepped in to treat an elephant calf that sustained a gunshot injury and was found in critical condition in the Herathgama Wildlife Zone.

title: Opposition MPs display Daily Mirror cartoon to protest against 22A
byline: As Opposition MPs held up posters featuring a Daily Mirror cartoon depicting President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, a tense situation erupted in Parliament today as they protested against the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution.

title: 22nd Amendment to Constitution presented to Parliament
byline: The Bill to amend the Constitution for the 22nd time and the Judicature Amendment Bill were presented to Parliament amid protests by the Opposition.

title: Former Fisheries Corporation chairman arrested
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has arrested former Fisheries Corporation Chairman Maheel Senaratne over allegations of irregularities in the procurement process related to fish sales centres established islandwide.

title: Dinesh Chandimal suffers injury, taken to hospital
byline: Dinesh Chandimal had to leave the field after sustaining an injury to his right shoulder and neck during the first session of Day 4 of the first Test against India.

title: Four Monaragala Crime Unit cops arrested over Rs. 500,000 ganja bribe
byline: A group of four police officers of the Monaragala Crime Investigation Unit were arrested last morning by Thanamalwila Police on suspicion of accepting a bribe of Rs.500,000 to dodge legal action against the owner of a ganja chena in Nikawewa area. Ganja or cannabis cultivation is unlawful in Sri Lanka

title: Sri Lankan government has sovereign rights to amend country’s laws: Justice Minister
byline: The government of Sri Lanka has the sovereign right to amend the country’s laws in line with the people’s mandate, Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara told Parliament today.

title: Underground clay pipe system unearthed at ancient Yapahuwa
byline: Archaeologists have uncovered important evidence of settlements and the daily lives of ordinary people during excavations at the historic Yapahuwa Kingdom under the Wayamba Project.

title: Dry spell hits some parts of Sri Lanka, water level drops in major tanks
byline: A dry spell in the Northern, Eastern and North Central provinces, as well as some areas of the Hambantota District, is reported, leading to water storage in more than 30 reservoirs and rivers falling to less than 50 per cent of their total capacity.

title: Global diesel price hike still a matter of concern for CPC
byline: The continuous rise of diesel is still a matter of concern for Sri Lanka, an official said yesterday.

title: Kandy Esala Perahera kicks off today
byline: The Kandy Sri Dalada Maligawa Esala Perahera will parade the streets tonight.

title: Water Board turns to groundwater to face dry weather
byline: Amidst predictions that Sri Lanka will have to face severe dry weather in the first quarter of 2027 due to the El Niño phenomenon, the National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) is taking steps to strengthen the groundwater section in addition to the surface water, NWSDB Chairman Chandana Bandara said yesterday.

title: Drug shortage puts cancer patients’ lives at stake
byline: Cancer patients receiving treatment at Apeksha Hospital in Maharagama have appealed to the authorities to urgently address shortages of essential medicines, warning that delays in treatment could put their lives at risk.

title: Keheliya appears before Bribery Commission in wheelchair
byline: Former Health Minister Keheliya Rambukwella recently appeared before the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) in a wheelchair to provide a statement in connection with an ongoing investigation.

title: Controversial 22nd Amendment to Constitution to be presented in Parliament today
byline: The Twenty-Second Amendment to the Constitution Bill, which is at the centre of controversy, will be presented to Parliament today, opening the door to legal battles.

title: US states call for big changes to Instagram and Facebook as Meta child privacy trial begins
byline: Meta has been hit with successive losses in court over how its platforms have targeted and harmed young users, but a jury trial set to begin on Tuesday may pose the biggest threat yet to its operations.

title: Two dead in school shooting in southern Philippines
byline: A student was shot dead at a high school in the southern Philippines before the alleged killer took his own life, the local mayor said, in the second school shooting in the South-east Asian nation in two months.

title: Warm weather advisory for Eastern Province, seven districts
byline: The Meteorology Department has issued a Warm Weather Advisory for Wednesday (19), warning that the heat index could reach the ‘Caution’ level in parts of the Eastern Province and seven districts.

title: G.L. Peiris files another petition against 22nd Amendment
byline: Former Minister, former Dean of the Faculty of Law and former Vice Chancellor of the University of Colombo, Prof. G.L. Peiris, today filed another Special Determination petition in the Supreme Court challenging the constitutionality of the Bill titled the “Twenty-Second Amendment to the Constitution.”

title: The Milky Way devoured a smaller galaxy about 11.8 billion years ago
byline: The Milky Way, a large and spiral-shaped galaxy that is home to hundreds of billions of stars including our sun, has taken a long and ​complicated path to achieve its current dimensions, as illustrated by new research documenting a milestone event early in its history.

title: Health Ministry seeks solution to Muslim nurses’ uniform concerns
byline: The Ministry of Health has taken steps to find an immediate and permanent solution to concerns over the official uniforms worn by Muslim female nursing officers at Kalmunai Hospital and other hospitals.

title: British couple on honeymoon killed in helicopter crash on Greek island
byline: A young British couple and their pilot were killed in a helicopter crash on the Greek island of Sifnos on Monday, Greek police have said.

title: Tourism activities at Nildiya Pokuna to come under Wildlife Department regulation
byline: Tourism activities at Nildiya Pokuna, located within the Ravana Ella Sanctuary, are to be formally regulated and conducted under the supervision of the Wildlife Conservation Department.

title: YouTube changes how views are counted: What it means for creators
byline: YouTube is changing the way it counts public views across videos, shorts and live streams, with a view set to count from the moment playback begins. The change will standardise view counting across formats and help creators better understand their overall exposure.

title: Cabinet approves Inter-Ministerial Committee on Human Rights
byline: The Cabinet has approved the establishment of an Inter-Ministerial Standing Committee on Human Rights to strengthen Sri Lanka’s national mechanism for monitoring and reporting on human rights.

title: Rs. 5,000 allowance for over 5,000 special-needs students
byline: The Cabinet has approved a proposal to provide a monthly allowance of Rs. 5,000 to students with special educational needs from low-income families.

title: Sri Lanka moves to replace Prevention of Terrorism Act
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the publication and subsequent submission to Parliament of a new Bill titled the “Protection of the State from Terrorism Act”, aimed at replacing the existing Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act, No. 48 of 1979.

title: BASL takes 22nd amendment battle to Supreme Court
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has filed a Special Determination petition before the Supreme Court challenging the constitutionality of the Bill titled “Twenty-Second Amendment to the Constitution,” which proposes to increase the retirement age of Supreme Court judges to 67 and Court of Appeal judges to 65.

title: Digital IDs planned by next year
byline: Digital Economy Deputy Minister Eranga Weeraratne said the Government plans to introduce digital National Identity Cards (NICs) within the next few years, eventually replacing the existing identity cards currently used by the public.

title: Pakistan top court orders ex-PM Imran Khan be moved to hospital from jail, his party says
byline: The Supreme Court of Pakistan ordered on Tuesday that former Prime Minister Imran Khan ​be moved to hospital from jail, his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party ‌said, meeting a longstanding demand of his party and family, who had raised concerns about his health.

title: Special programme launched to distribute drinking water in drought-hit districts
byline: A special programme has been launched to distribute drinking water to people in districts including Batticaloa, Monaragala and Ampara, which are currently experiencing dry weather conditions, the President’s Media Division (PMD) said.

title: Sri Lanka, Poland approve extradition agreement
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to sign an agreement between Sri Lanka and the Republic of Poland on the extradition of offenders.

title: Canada braces for 50% US tariffs, with negotiators still far apart
byline: Canada faces a new round of 50% U.S. tariffs this ​week that businesses said could cause job losses in some already struggling industries, while complicating broader negotiations over the future of North America’s free trade agreement.

title: Sri Lanka to implement national pharmaceutical policy 2026-2030
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the expedited implementation of Sri Lanka’s National Pharmaceutical Policy for 2026-2030, aimed at ensuring access to safe, effective, quality and affordable essential medicines for the entire population.

title: Doctors remove 3.1kg stone from man’s bladder and claim record
byline: Doctors in Sri Lanka have removed a 3.1kg (6.8lb) bladder stone from a man - which they believe to be the largest of its kind on record.

title: Education Council to be established in Sri Lanka
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the preparation of a Bill to establish an Education Council to standardize, register, license, assure quality and accredit professionals in the general education sector.

title: Zambia’s President Hakainde Hichilema wins second term
byline: Zambia’s President Hakainde Hichilema ⁠has won re-election for ⁠a second five-year term, according to the electoral authorities, after a race marred by allegations of fraud.

title: How do NPP Ministers predict my verdict before court? – asks Namal
byline: SLPP Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa has questioned how NPP ministers could predict that he would be sentenced to prison when the court has yet to deliver its verdict.

title: Strong winds, rough seas expected along Sri Lanka coast
byline: The Department of Meteorology has issued an advisory warning of strong winds and rough seas in several sea areas around Sri Lanka.

title: CSE slides on heavy selling as ASPI falls below 21,500
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange came under notable selling pressure on Tuesday, 18 August 2026, with both benchmark indices closing firmly lower as weakness spread across the broader market.

title: Former Fisheries Corporation chairman remanded after failing to meet bail conditions
byline: Former Chairman of the Ceylon Fisheries Corporation Mahil Senaratne, who was granted bail after being arrested by the Bribery Commission, was remanded today (18) after failing to fulfil the bail conditions imposed by court.

title: Govt denies claims of LTTE training camp operating in Pallai
byline: Claims circulating on social media that an LTTE terrorist training camp is operating within the Pallai forest reserve are completely false, Cabinet Spokesman Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said today (18).

title: Ven. Rambukana Siddhartha Thero passes away
byline: Veteran Buddhist monk, renowned lyricist and author Ven. Rambukana Siddhartha Thero has passed away at the age of 76.

title: Huge challenge before SL to avoid another economic crisis: Ranil
byline: Sri Lanka is facing a huge challenge to prevent another economic crisis in 2027/28 as it has to find funds to start repaying its debts, former President Ranil Wickremesinghe said today.

title: Ukraine fires nearly 800 drones at Russia in one of war’s biggest attacks
byline: Ukraine launched one of its biggest drone attacks on Russia since Moscow’s invasion more than four years ago, firing almost 800 drones overnight, officials said on Tuesday. The strike came just two days after a similar barrage, as both sides stepped up long-range attacks far from the front line.

title: Major reservoirs hold 37.2% of effective storage capacity
byline: Sri Lanka’s 74 major reservoirs held a total of 1.106 million acre-feet of effective water storage as of August 16, Director of Irrigation (Water Management), Eng. H.M.P.S.D. Herath said.

title: ADB provides US$200 million for post-Ditwah recovery
byline: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has provided a US$200 million loan to Sri Lanka to support reconstruction and livelihood recovery following Cyclone Ditwah.

title: Government will not confront UN
byline: The government does not intend to confront the United Nations (UN) over the comments made by its Special Rapporteur on the 20th Amendment, Leader of the House Bimal Ratnayake told Parliament today.

title: Ex-Australia batter Warner fined for drink-driving
byline: The 39-year-old’s blood alcohol reading was more than twice the legal limit as he failed a random breath test when driving his family home from a social function.

title: Keheliya Rambukwella released on bail
byline: Former Minister Keheliya Rambukwella was today (18) ordered to be released on bail by the Colombo Magistrate’s Court in connection with a corruption case filed against him by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC).

title: UAE air defences detect missile threat; residents told situation is safe
byline: UAE authorities have reassured residents that the situation in the country is currently safe after air defence systems responded to a missile threat directed towards the UAE.

title: Cancer patients at risk amid reported shortage of G-CSF drugs: Specialist
byline: Cancer patients are being placed at risk due to an alleged shortage of essential drugs used to boost immunity and increase white blood cell levels during cancer treatment, Dr. Sanjeewa, of the Doctors’ Trade Union Alliance for Medical and Civil Rights Chairman Specialist Dr. Chamal Sanjeewa said.
